bull_bear.body: Liquidity increased by INR 70 Cr in FY26; No dividends mentioned; Focus on reinvestment for growth and potential M&A integration readiness; Management increasing skin-in-game via ESOPs.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical instability in Middle East (31% revenue exposure) causing contracting delays; Customer concentration (Top 10 = 60%); Hardware availability (GPUs) for AI product deployment; Lack of promoter holding (diverse retail base).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and assertive on turnaround completion; Acknowledges stock undervaluation; Transparent about Middle East risks but emphasizes mitigation via offshoring; Bullish on FY27 conversion.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly states the market has not caught up with fundamentals; AI is viewed as a 'tailwind' enhancing their System of Record rather than a disruptor; Goodwill of INR 190 Cr+ passed impairment test despite past concerns.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance-sheet liquidity is the deck's stated capital-allocation message: cash and cash equivalents stood at Rs 18,480 lakhs as on 30th Jun 2026 versus Rs 17,526 lakhs on 31st March 2026, "reflecting continued liquidity stability".
- The same cash position is restated in the business highlights as "healthy at Rs 184.8 Cr".
- No dividend, buyback, debt or reinvestment/capex policy is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Over three decades of telecom domain expertise underpinning its solution portfolio
- AI, GenAI and advanced-analytics capability embedded across Business Assurance, Fraud Management and Partner Ecosystem Management
- Long-standing relationships with several of the world's leading telecommunications companies
- Recognised for the second consecutive year in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI in CSP Customer and Business Operations
- Broad, integrated portfolio spanning assurance, fraud, partner management, managed services and consulting that addresses an estimated US$4.3 billion addressable market
- Lightweight, plug-and-play deployment model (FraudZap) enabling faster implementation and time-to-value versus traditional fraud management deployments
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Foreign exchange risk from export concentration — A significant portion of revenue is derived from international markets - exports contributed 99% of total turnover - exposing the Company to currency fluctuations, particularly USD/INR, which may impact profitability and cash flows; mitigated through a calibrated hedging strategy that maintains prudent hedge coverage on net foreign currency exposure while retaining flexibility to benefit from favourable moves.
- Talent and capability risk in an AI-scarce labour market — Rapid adoption of AI and digital technologies has intensified competition for specialised talent, and the ability to attract, develop and retain skilled professionals is critical to sustaining innovation and execution; permanent-employee turnover was 22% in FY26 (24% FY25, 33% FY24). Mitigation includes building an AI-native workforce through targeted capability development, GenAI-enabled engineering practices, Code Shield workshops and adoption of GitHub Copilot.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy — Increasing cyber threats, evolving data privacy regulations and rising expectations on responsible AI usage elevate compliance and security requirements; failure to address them could impact customer trust, reputation and business performance. BRSR identifies Data Privacy and Security as a material risk, given regulatory penalties, legal liabilities, operational disruption and reputational damage from non-compliance or cyber incidents.
- Technology disruption and competitive intensity / market positioning — Rapid advances in AI platforms and managed agent ecosystems may alter customer preferences, while established global players, niche providers, hyperscalers and emerging AI-native companies compete for the same customers; intensifying competition may affect new-customer acquisition, retention, pricing and market share. Mitigation is continuous benchmarking plus a balanced mix of proprietary innovation and selected third-party AI capabilities.
- AI infrastructure availability (GPU supply) — Growing demand for GenAI solutions increases dependence on specialised computing infrastructure including GPUs; supply constraints and extended procurement lead times may affect product development and customer deployments. Mitigated by optimising solution architectures, using a mix of on-premise and cloud infrastructure, and deploying open-source AI models for selected use cases.
- Project execution and supply chain dependency on customer readiness — Delays in customer-side infrastructure readiness and extended hardware procurement cycles may affect implementation timelines; addressed via cloud-based deployment alternatives, embedding infrastructure-readiness requirements in project planning, and working with approved vendor ecosystems.
- Customer capital-expenditure discipline and demand deferral — The telecom industry operates under disciplined capital allocation; during periods of constrained capex, CSPs may defer or reprioritise investments in digital transformation, operational modernisation and business support platforms, directly affecting demand for Subex's software and business assurance platforms. CSPs are expected to remain selective, prioritising spend that delivers measurable improvements.
- Geopolitical and regional business risk — Geopolitical tensions, regional conflicts, trade restrictions and evolving regulatory landscapes may delay customer investment decisions, disrupt project execution and create demand volatility across geographies; restrictions on cross-border operations and supply chains may hinder implementation and technology deployment.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "The Subex Advantage" is framed on six pillars: Geography Focus, Strong Annuity Model, Landed and Expanding, Few Players with Data Access, Strong Tailwinds in AI, and Telco Domain Expertise.
- Moat is stated as data access plus stickiness: "Large customer base with data connectors processing 200bn+ records per instance" and "High switching costs".
- Revenue quality is annuity-led: "Strong revenue model with ~70% revenue is annuity/recurring nature" and "Excellent customer retention of ~92%".
- Geography focus is dual-track: "Revenue growth driven by strong presence in emerging markets and increased AI adoption in developed markets", with a "Global Marquee Customer Base" across Americas, EMEA and Asia.
- Domain depth is claimed as "30+ years of expertise in telecom and handling Telco data across functions".

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Subex sells AI-led software and services to Communications Service Providers (CSPs) and other telecom operators, spanning Business Assurance, Fraud Management, Partner Ecosystem Management, Managed Services and Business Consulting. The Company combines deep telecom domain expertise with artificial intelligence and advanced analytics so operators can protect revenues, manage operational complexity and strengthen digital confidence across interconnected telecom ecosystems. Revenue is earned through support and other services, license/implementation & customisation, and managed services, with almost all of it coming from customers outside India.

- **Partner Ecosystem Management:** Partner Lifecycle Management, Digital Services Billing, Wholesale Billing & Routing, Enterprise Billing, Roaming Settlements
- **Managed Services & Consulting:** Managed Services, Consulting & Advisory Services

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Enter FY27 driving three priorities: grow the core telco business faster, expand the AI product portfolio in fraud management and agentic operations, and convert early-stage contracts into recurring revenue at scale
- Reposition Subex from a legacy RAFM vendor into the intelligence layer for the telecom industry, articulated through the 'New Possibilities Now Possible' brand identity unveiled at the Global User Conference in Athens in November 2025
- Establish category leadership in Telecom AI within the three-to-five-year window management believes is open
- Build fast and deploy early against emerging fraud types - identify the problem early, build fast, deploy, and stay with the customer (the model used for FraudZap)
- Embed AI, GenAI and advanced analytics across the flagship HyperSense and ROC platforms and the Business Assurance portfolio, moving customers from reactive to predictive, outcome-driven assurance
- Deploy domain-trained, LLM-powered AI Agents that automate fraud investigation and assurance workflows, with defined success metrics and structured paths to full deployment
- Defend the moat built on high switching costs, proprietary data compounding daily and 30 years of embedded domain expertise, where every new customer improves the models
- Expand into telecom adjacencies - mobile money, fintech, IoT, MVNO/MVNE services and digital infrastructure - which require specialised fraud prevention, assurance and risk management
- Sustain the operating discipline of the last three years: cost structure of talent, product focus and customer discipline, now investing from strength rather than necessity
- Embed responsible AI - explainability, auditability and bias-control mechanisms - and a cloud-native, demand-elastic platform architecture that lowers the environmental footprint of AI workloads
- Committed to achieving Net-Zero emissions by the year 2035, covering Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions
- ISO 27001:2013 adopted and mapped to responsible consumer engagement (P9); ISO standards mapped to integrity, sustainable products, stakeholder responsiveness and an EMS as part of ISO for environment
- Board-approved policies covering all nine NGRBC principles, translated into procedures and extended to value chain partners
- Progress against sustainability commitments reviewed through a structured approach led by committees and overseen by Management and the Board of Directors
- Data privacy and security programme strengthened during the year through enhanced vulnerability management, timely patching, continuous security monitoring, employee security awareness and phishing simulations, expanded passwordless authentication across Subex applications and stronger encryption controls
- Employee well-being addressed through periodic employee connects and access to well-being tools such as an Employee Assistance Programme, plus periodic health and safety awareness and safety camps
- Grievance redressal via a Subex Global Whistle-blowing Policy available to communities, employees, workers and value chain partners, and an investor grievance channel through investorrelations@subex.com and SEBI SCORES
- Women constituted 16.7% of the Board of Directors and 32.4% of total employees as at the end of FY26
- CSR under section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 is not applicable to the Company
- Sustainability disclosures are made on a standalone basis for Indian operations and have not been subjected to independent external assurance (no assurance provider appointed)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no plant, capacity, capex project, delivery-centre addition, acquisition or JV. Subex is an asset-light telecom software company and its expansion narrative is product- and market-led rather than capacity-led: the Company describes building out its portfolio of Fraud Management, Business Assurance, Partner Ecosystem Management, Managed Services and Business Consulting Services around the HyperSense, ROC, FraudZap and AI Agent Squad platforms, and during FY26 continued to embed AI and advanced analytics across the Business Assurance portfolio to move customers from reactive assurance to predictive, outcome-driven assurance. On market footprint, management states the addressable market for what Subex does was $0.19 billion three years ago and is $4.3 billion today, with expansion opportunities in telecom adjacencies such as mobile money, fintech, IoT, MVNO/MVNE services and digital infrastructure. No commissioning dates, capacity figures or capital-expenditure plans of the Company itself are disclosed in this text; the only capital-expenditure discussion relates to customers' (CSPs') network spending, which management flags as a demand risk when constrained.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global telecom industry is shifting from connectivity to intelligence, with operators monetising digital infrastructure through AI, cloud, advanced analytics and data centres as 5G investments mature
- Global Telecom Outlook projects global telecommunications revenues to reach approximately US$1.32 trillion by 2029, a CAGR of 2.8%
- Subex's addressable market expanded from approximately US$0.19 billion to approximately US$4.3 billion over three years
- Telecom industry loses US$42 billion annually to fraud, equal to 2.46% of revenues, and that loss is growing at nearly six times the rate of industry revenue itself
- Device fraud was the single largest fraud type in 2025, accounting for 10% of all global fraud losses
- CSPs are diversifying into IoT, enterprise connectivity, private 5G, cloud services, fintech and mobile money, content platforms and API-driven services, creating far greater operational complexity across networks, billing, partner management and revenue assurance
- Operators are shifting from rule-based fraud systems to intelligent, continuously learning platforms capable of real-time detection and prevention
- Agentic AI is enabling operators to automate investigation, assurance, partner management and operational workflows
- Rise of AI-generated identities, voice cloning and deepfake-enabled fraud is increasing demand for advanced authentication and identity verification
- Growing emphasis on digital sovereignty, data privacy, cybersecurity resilience and responsible AI governance is reshaping enterprise technology priorities
- Enterprise spending on strategic technology initiatives remained resilient despite inflationary pressures, geopolitical developments, trade dynamics and regulatory change
- Telecom operators are expected to maintain investments in initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, strengthen digital trust, enable service innovation and support business transformation
- Constrained telecom capital expenditure could cause CSPs to defer or reprioritise digital transformation and business support platform investments, affecting demand
- Revenue mix commentary: Support & others continues to be the largest revenue contributor, followed by License, Implementation & customisation and Managed services
- India is strengthening its position as a global innovation hub for next-generation telecom and digital technologies, supported by digital public infrastructure, deep technology talent and nationwide 5G rollout
- More than 80% of new business wins in FY26 incorporated AI use cases
- Near-complete renewal success across strategic customer accounts; 92% of customers renewed with value retention of 98%
- FraudZap was built and contracted within six months of inception
- Early-stage contracts are to be converted into recurring revenue at scale as an FY27 priority
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Subex has completed its operational reset with 3 consecutive quarters of positive PAT and a 24% YoY order intake growth, signaling a shift from defense to offense. While FY26 revenue grew only 6% due to base effects from non-core exits, the strong backlog and successful AI product commercialization (FraudZap) position FY27 for accelerated conversion, though Middle East geopolitical risks remain a monitored variable.

open.item: Subex will pursue three priorities in FY27: grow the core telco business faster, expand its AI product portfolio in fraud management and agentic operations, and convert early-stage contracts into recurring revenue at scale.

The Company is focused on helping customers harness AI to automate risk, strengthen digital trust and simplify operational complexity, anchored in its vision of enabling businesses to become fearless, seamless and fraud-free by design.
Management states the window to establish category leadership in Telecom AI is open for three to five years and the Company is pursuing it with everything it has.
Domain-trained, LLM-powered AI Agents automating fraud investigation and assurance workflows are running on production-grade data with defined success metrics and structured paths to full deployment.

Management flags that during periods of constrained capital expenditure CSPs may defer or reprioritise investments in digital transformation and business support platforms, affecting demand for Subex's software.
